planting.note: Set container plants into consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade in early spring or fall; this Walters Gardens release is one of several Bouquet Perfect primroses in the series, alongside 'Rosalina', 'Violetta', and 'Scarletta'.

directions: Spearmint carries clusters of large white flowers washed with a cool mint-green cast over a tidy, rounded mound of crinkled foliage. Because the blooms are sterile, the plant keeps pushing out fresh flowers across the spring season rather than setting seed and fading. Keep the shallow root zone evenly moist and mulch in cold-winter zones to protect the crown. Works well massed under deciduous trees or in a shaded container display.

planting.note: Set container plants into consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade in early spring or fall; a Walters Gardens Bouquet Perfect series release.

directions: Violetta is the darkest-flowered member of the Bouquet Perfect series, with dark violet-blue blossoms packed tightly over a compact, well-rounded habit. Sterile flowers mean the plant channels its energy into continuous bloom rather than seed production through the spring. It prefers evenly moist, shaded ground and resents drying out, so a mulched woodland bed or shaded container suits it well. Pair with chartreuse-leaved companions to set off the intense flower color.

planting.note: Set container plants into consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade in early spring or fall; part of the Walters Gardens Bouquet Perfect lineup.

directions: Scarletta brings saturated red blooms to the shade garden, held low over a dense rosette of dark green, crinkled leaves. Like its series siblings, the sterile flowers extend the bloom window through early, mid, and late spring instead of setting seed. Give it reliably moist, shaded soil, since the shallow roots dry out quickly in a sunny or exposed spot. A good edging plant along shaded walkways or at the front of a woodland border.

subcategory: shade-tolerant spiderwort with oversized blue flowers

planting.note: Divide or plant container stock in spring into average, well-drained garden soil in sun to shade; a Walters Gardens release bred as a companion to 'Webmaster'.

directions: Web Designer forms a thick, leafy clump topped with exceptionally large flowers for a spiderwort, in clear blue. Unlike many Tradescantia selections that go ragged in summer heat, this one holds its foliage and continues flowering well into fall. It tolerates everything from full sun to fairly deep shade, making it a flexible filler for mixed borders or woodland edges. Cut plants back hard after the first flush if they start to sprawl, and they will rebloom from the base.

subcategory: part-shade tropical aroid with variegated foliage

planting.note: Move divisions or container plants outdoors after last frost into rich, moist, well-drained soil in part sun to light shade; a 2006 Asiatica Nursery (Barry Yinger) introduction currently carried at retail by Plant Delights Nursery.

directions: Moon Landing is a variegated sport of the familiar hooded Chinese taro, its glossy leaves marked chartreuse-gold and mottled green instead of the usual solid green. It builds a dense clump of upright, heart-shaped foliage that reads well as a specimen in a shaded bed or large container. Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged, and bring pots indoors well before frost in all but the mildest zones. Feed monthly during the growing season to keep the variegated leaves from reverting.

subcategory: part-shade calla lily with deep red spathes

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions 2-3 inches deep in moist, organically rich soil in part sun to light shade after danger of frost has passed; a Plant Delights Nursery introduction.

directions: Frozen Queen produces deep cherry-red spathes with the rich cast of a good Bordeaux wine around a pale central spadix, held above glossy, white-speckled arrow-shaped leaves. It flowers reliably in the cooler light of a part-shade bed, where the saturated color reads well against lighter-leaved companions. Keep the rhizomes in evenly moist, rich soil through the growing season, and lift them in cold zones before the ground freezes. Combine with ferns or hostas for a richly colored shade planting.

subcategory: cold-hardy dwarf palm for shaded gardens

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring into moist to wet, humus-rich soil in sun to light shade; a narrow-leaflet strain collected in 2006 near Pittsview, Russell County, Alabama, and released by Plant Delights Nursery/JLBG.

directions: Pittsview is a narrow-leaflet selection of the trunkless dwarf palmetto chosen for its toughness in cooler climates than most palms can survive, growing as an understory plant from shaded woodland edges to open ground. Its blue-green, fan-shaped leaves emerge in a slow-growing clump directly from ground level with little to no visible trunk. It establishes slowly and transplants poorly once rooted in the landscape, so start with container stock and leave it undisturbed. Useful as a long-lived structural accent at the back of a shaded native planting.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

subcategory: part-shade bulb with late-summer pink flower stalks

planting.note: Plant bulbs with the neck at or just below soil level in well-drained, humus-rich soil in part sun to light shade; a selection of the Lycoris sprengeri x radiata hybrid from Plant Delights Nursery.

directions: Hazuki Elegance sends up bare, leafless flower stalks in late summer carrying clusters of rosy-pink blooms dramatically tipped in blue, well ahead of the strap-like foliage that follows in fall. As a selection of the naturally occurring rosea hybrid, it tends toward slightly refined flower form compared to the species. Plant bulbs in light shade under deciduous trees where summer dormancy goes unnoticed, and avoid summer irrigation once foliage dies back. Leave clumps undisturbed for years, since flowering improves as bulbs multiply.

subcategory: tall part-shade monkshood with blue-violet spires

planting.note: Divide tuberous roots or plant container stock in spring into moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in sun to light shade; collected at roughly 4,200 ft near Kupres, Bosnia in 2012 by Tony Avent and Hans Hansen, released by Plant Delights Nursery.

directions: Kupres is a selection of the Balkan monkshood named for the Bosnian plateau where it was collected, sending up tall, dense spires of hooded blue-violet flowers in late summer over dark green, deeply cut foliage. It performs best in cool, evenly moist soil with some afternoon shade, and resents both drought and being moved once settled. Site it toward the back of a border where its height can stand without staking. All parts are highly toxic if ingested or handled with broken skin, so place it away from pets and small children.

subcategory: part-shade native wildflower with vivid scarlet flowers

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring into average to rocky, well-drained, acidic soil in part sun to light shade; a patented (PP36,247) native selection from Plant Delights Nursery.

directions: Forged by Fire is a selected form of the eastern native fire pink, chosen for an especially saturated, hot-scarlet flower color held on wiry stems above a low mat of foliage. It suits a lightly shaded rock garden or woodland edge, where hummingbirds reliably visit the tubular blooms. Give it sharp drainage and some relief from the hottest afternoon sun, since the species naturally grows on rocky slopes and open woodland margins. Treat it as a short-lived perennial that self-sows modestly where happy, refreshing the planting over time.

common_name: Fall in Love Deeply Japanese Anemone
subcategory: part-shade fall-blooming anemone with rose-pink flowers

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in full sun to part shade; a Walters Gardens release in the Fall in Love series.

directions: Deeply carries deep rose-pink, saucer-shaped flowers on wiry stems above mounded, dark green foliage from late summer into fall, well after most perennials have finished. Unlike some Japanese anemones that run aggressively, this selection spreads slowly by rhizome, making it easier to place in a mixed border without it taking over. It tolerates a good deal of shade and appreciates afternoon relief in hot climates, along with steady moisture through the growing season. Let clumps stand through winter for structure and cut back in early spring.
